idea: A web application for families to assign recurring household tasks, attach evidence, and fairly resolve completion disputes.

answers.answer: Parents and teenagers in one household use it. Parents manage membership; everyone can receive and complete tasks.
A member creates or receives a task, completes it, attaches a photo or note as evidence, and the assigner accepts it or opens a dispute.
A task is complete only when required evidence is attached and accepted. Every status change must be visible to the household.
Tasks can repeat daily, weekly, or on selected weekdays, with the next occurrence created automatically.
Only parents invite or remove members. Members see only their household. Evidence must never be public.
Support 100 household members and 10,000 tasks per household; normal task pages should load within 2 seconds at p95.
Use email notifications for assignment, overdue tasks, and dispute decisions. No other integration is required for the first release.
No payments, rewards marketplace, public social feed, or native mobile app in the first release.
You decide the technical stack, but it must be a browser-based web application.

fallback: You decide that implementation detail. Keep the first release simple and testable.

concept.rationale: A browser-based first release avoids native-app scope while meeting the household workflow and email-notification needs.
